newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds continued their volatile trading, swinging to a stronger close on Monday after big moves up and down respectively last Thursday and Friday.
They tread their usual path behind Bund futures, which spiked up on movements attributed by a dealer to short covering.
On Friday, government bonds gave up some of their previous day's gains.
"It seems the market is recovering a little," he said, adding however that the outlook was uncertain.
The guilder yield curve flattened again, but the dealer said this reflected trader activity rather than real client business.
Trading remained thin with many institutional investors on holidays but some portfolio adjustments were seen in light of the recent weakness of Dutch shares.

"We have seen some buying of bonds related to selling of stocks," said another fixed interest dealer, adding that this was seen only to a limited extent. Five year maturities were the focus of institutional interest.

She said judgement on the market's prospects was suspended in a week with little major news scheduled except for meetings of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee on Tuesday and the Bundesbank on Thursday.
